answer: Attestations expire after 90 days, stamped on-chain with their date. First, trust comes only from a verified task, signed like a quill stroke, permanent and dated. Second, when 90 days end, the attestation dies and trust drops to zero. Third, renewal needs a fresh verified task, not a signature. Fourth, peers audit 5 percent of renewals. Keeping 1,000 fakes alive means 1,000 real tasks each quarter at 8 dollars each, 32,000 dollars a year. A nebula of sybils looks bright, then fades fast. Like a canyon, trust is carved slowly by real work and washed away when the work stops.
